title: Operation Pennywise: Sprint-by-sprint tracker for batching / cache / quant pilots
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Run a tightly-scoped set of parallel pilots (batching profiles, KV/prefix caching, and 4-bit quantization candidates) across representative workloads to achieve >=20% per-token cost reduction without >10% latency tail regressions or >2% QoQ metric degradation.

Scope: Three concurrent pilots, each with a defined owner: batching (SRE/serving runtime), cache (platform/infra), quantization (research/ops). Each pilot will run in prod-mirrored traffic using traffic shaping and canaries, with metric dashboards and automatic rollback hooks.

Success metrics: 
- Primary: percent reduction in per-token spend on dedicated/hosted workloads (target >=20%) measured over 2-week steady-state.
- Safety: P95 latency change <= +10% and error rate delta <= 0.5% for served routes.
- Quality: end-to-end task-level quality regression <= 2% on evaluative prompt set.
- Operational: clear playbooks for rollout, monitoring, and rollback; reproducible artifact set (benchmarks, config diffs, PRs).

Deliverables:
1) Pilot runbooks (one per pilot) with owners, rollout plan, rollback criteria.
2) Dashboards: cost-per-token, P50/P95 latency, error rate, prompt-set QA, model-version tracing.
3) Quantization artifacts: model/bitwidth matrix, benchmark harness, PRs to runtime.
4) Batching config matrix: policy files, throughput/latency tradeoff grid, suggested default profiles.
5) KV cache evaluation: hit-rate analysis, TTL heuristics, KV eviction policies, storage cost estimate.

Measurement plan: define control and treatment cohorts by route tag, capture token accounting via token-level attribution, run A/B tests for 14 days with automatic statistical checks. Link to measurement spec and dashboard in comments.

Rollout strategy: canary at 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated SLO gates. For Dedicated customers, run equivalent testing in dedicated slices with customer opt-in.

Risks & mitigations:
- Latency regressions from aggressive batching -> maintain low-latency profiles and prefer async batching for background routes.
- Quality loss from quantization -> only promote bitwidths with passing eval thresholds and shadow inference comparisons.
- Cache correctness -> implement cache validation layer and observe cache hit correlations with request success.

Decision log (summary):
- 2026-02-17: Chose 4-bit quant candidates with per-layer mixed precision as first pass (PM/Research) after bench tests.
- 2026-02-21: Agreed to instrument token-level accounting in runtime-1.22 (Engineering) before treatment rollout.
- 2026-03-03: Moved batching pilot to flow-based policies after latency microbench flagged worst-case tail on long-context routes.

Next actions (owner tagged):
- ENG-21312 (Brian): finalize canary automation and SLO gates by 2026-03-10.
- ENG-21345 (SRE): KV cache TTL tuning and dashboard by 2026-03-14.
- DES-1789 (Design): dashboard UX and prompt-set test harness by 2026-03-09.

Notes: This ticket is the cross-functional tracker for the sprint; operational checkpoints should be created as child issues for any actionable engineering work that exceeds 2 days of effort.
